title: Finite exchange and counit restrictions form strict isomorphism towers
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For a scheme $W$, write $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ on the small pro-etale site $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the strict derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_W}(A_n)_W$, and exact restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Let $Rf_*$ be the tower direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

For a geometric point $y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], set $S=X\times_Ys$ with projections $v:S\to X$, $h:S\to s$ [def-pc-base-change], and $P_y=\{x:s\to X\mid fx=y\}$. For $x\in P_y$ let $i_x:s\to S$ be the unique lift, so $vi_x=x$ and $hi_x=\operatorname{id}_s$. This is a finite set; an empty sum indexed by $P_y$ is the zero object. Write $L(-)^*$ for the completed integral pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and $(-)_n^*$ for its exact finite-coefficient inverse image.

Fix $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and one flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to K$, with strict quotients $Q_n=Q\otimes_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ and quotient maps $Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. There are specified maps of strict coefficient-system complexes on $s$:
$$B_n=y_n^*f_{*,n}Q_n\xrightarrow{b_n}C_n=h_{*,n}v_n^*Q_n\xrightarrow{r_n}D_n=\bigoplus_{x\in P_y}x_n^*Q_n.$$
The first is the exchange map defined by the pullback/direct-image adjunction counit. The $x$-component of the second is $i_{x,n}^*$ of the counit $h_n^*h_{*,n}v_n^*Q_n\to v_n^*Q_n$, with $hi_x=\operatorname{id}_s$; thus it sends a section to its germ at $i_x$. The maps preserve addition and the $A_n$-action. For each $n$ their two squares with the quotient transitions commute as maps of complexes, before passing to derived categories. They are natural in maps of representatives and determine natural maps of derived coefficient systems independent of the chosen representative.

Every evaluated $b_n$ and $r_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Under etale/pro-etale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] they are the canonical etale finite exchange and geometric-stalk restriction maps, with the direct-image comparison normalized as the counit mate. Sheaves on $s_{\mathrm{et}}$ are identified with their sections at $s$, and the summands are the individual point restrictions. All finite direct images occurring here, on both sites, are exact, so termwise maps compute the derived maps. In particular the two maps of restricted strict towers are isomorphisms in their derived category, and their total derived inverse limits are isomorphisms [def-weil-derived-limit, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: The base change $h:S\to s$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$), so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $Y$ locally Noetherian. A finite map is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and the definition of properness; hence [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] applies to $f$ and to $h$, whose target is $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus both are locally of finite presentation. Finiteness also makes both maps quasi-compact and quasi-separated, since they are proper. The points $i_x$ correspond bijectively to the $x$ in the statement by the universal property of $S$. Finiteness of $P_y$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction], applied to $f$ at $y$; this assertion concerns the index set, independently of the input sheaf. The Lean helper finitePoints identifies its reducible Points subtype with Scheme.Hom.GeometricFiber and directly reuses the existing GeometricFiber.finite instance, independently of the stalk formula.

source.place: Tags 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite), 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), 01T6; finite presentation over a locally Noetherian target; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03QP

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-finite-fp-proetale-pushforward-exact] to $f,h$: it gives exactness on the entire finite-coefficient module categories on the pro-etale sites. On the etale sites [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] gives exactness on underlying abelian sheaves; the identical module kernels and cokernels give exactness for $A_n$-modules. Every finite-coefficient inverse image used here is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identifies the termwise direct images and inverse images with their derived functors, even for an unbounded representative. In particular this applies to $Q_n$ and $v_n^*Q_n$. The resolution and reduction construction of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] identifies $Q_n$ with the derived reduction $K_n$. The helper push_additive already follows without finiteness from the existing right-adjoint structure of integralComparisonSequenceDirectImage: a right adjoint preserves binary products, and an additive-category functor preserving binary products is additive. The pointSum_additive helper is proved by composing with its jointly monic product projections, whose component pullback functors are additive. The strict-system helper pushExact is proved by forgetting module structure, restricting to each vertical coefficient slice, and applying the abelian-sheaf exactness of lem-zl-finite-fp-proetale-pushforward-exact. Vertical slice restriction is a left adjoint because the slice inclusion is cocontinuous, so it preserves epimorphisms. The image sieve of the whole sequence direct-image map pulls back on each vertical slice to the image sieve of this levelwise direct image. Thus these image sieves cover by the definition of coefficientSequenceTopology, giving local surjectivity and an epimorphism on abelian sheaves. The faithful forgetful functor reflects epimorphisms and preserves them by lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful. The existing right-adjoint structure gives finite limits; preservation of epimorphisms and kernels then gives homology preservation and finite colimits. No nonempty-fibre hypothesis is used.

Use the module adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] on each small pro-etale site. For an $A_n$-module sheaf $M$, the adjoint defining exchange is
$$h_n^*y_n^*f_{*,n}M\simeq v_n^*f_n^*f_{*,n}M\xrightarrow{v_n^*\varepsilon_{f,n,M}}v_n^*M.$$
Its transpose is $b_{n,M}$. Define $r_{n,x,M}$ by applying $i_{x,n}^*$ to $\varepsilon_{h,n,v_n^*M}$, identifying $(hi_x)_n^*$ with the identity and $(vi_x)_n^*$ with $x_n^*$. The inverse-image and direct-image constructions in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] show the counit explicitly: a local inverse-image representative $[V,\phi,m]$, with $m\in M(X\times_YV)$, is sent to its restriction along $\phi$. In the module tensor notation this sends $a\otimes[V,\phi,m]$ to $a(m|_\phi)$. Therefore $r_{n,x}$ is restriction at $i_x$. These formulas are additive and $A_n$-linear. Apply them in each degree to $M=Q_n^j$. Naturality for the differential $d^j$ makes them chain maps, and their finite tuple is the stated map to the direct sum.

source.place: Tags 03D6 (definition-pushforward), 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules); sites.tex Section 06UM (section-pullback), evaluation counit on colimit representatives

proof.text:
Write $t_n:Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$ for the actual quotient map. Regard its target as an $A_{n+1}$-module via $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Direct image is evaluation on the same fibre products, so it commutes literally with this scalar restriction. Since pullback of a constant coefficient ring is the same constant ring, inverse image after scalar restriction is the same underlying inverse image with the restricted action. The counit formula in Step 3 is unchanged under this identification: restricting the coefficient ring changes only the action, and
$$t_n(a(m|_\phi))=\bar a\,(t_n(m)|_\phi).$$
Here $\bar a$ is the image in $A_n$ of a local $A_{n+1}$-coefficient; this identity follows from linearity of $t_n$ and its compatibility with restrictions. Taking the transpose in the displayed exchange adjunction, or using its restriction formula on $[V,\phi,m]$, gives
$$C(t_n)b_{n+1}=b_nB(t_n),\qquad D(t_n)r_{n+1}=r_nC(t_n).$$
These are equalities of chain maps. The same identity works for arbitrary successive quotients. Finally restriction to $R_s$ makes all transitions and both families $R_s$-linear, since $R_s\to(A_n)_s$ factors through $(A_{n+1})_s$ as specified in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. This constructs the two maps of strict restricted towers. In Lean, transitionSquares follows degreewise from naturality of coefficientSequenceTransition, applied to the components of the strict chain maps b and r; HomologicalComplex.hom_ext combines the degreewise equations.

source.place: Tags 03D6 and 03D7, explicit action and counit; proetale.tex Tag 09A5 (section-morphism); strict quotient transitions in def-pur-integral-derived-operations

proof.text: Fix $n$. By the definition of $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the reduction $K_n$ has bounded constructible cohomology. The ring $A_n$ is finite and hence Noetherian, and $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by its separated finite-type hypothesis. Therefore [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] gives a bounded constructible etale complex $L_n$ and an isomorphism $\alpha_n:\nu_X^*L_n\simeq K_n$. This choice is only for proving invertibility and identifying arrows in the derived category; no etale origin of each individual term $Q_n^j$ is asserted.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-discrete-exchange-site-comparison] with $\Lambda=A_n$, $g=y$, $f'=h$, $g'=v$ and $L=L_n$. Step 1 checks its quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses for $f,h$; $L_n$ is bounded below. The derived exchange $e^p$ is the mate, for $Lf_n^*\dashv Rf_{*,n}$ and $Lh_n^*\dashv Rh_{*,n}$, of the composition comparison $h_n^*y_n^*\simeq v_n^*f_n^*$; all four functors are exact (Step 2). Hence [lem-pur-exact-derived-mate], with $L=f_n^*$, $L'=h_n^*$, $G=y_n^*$, $H=v_n^*$ and $\sigma$ that termwise comparison, shows that $e^p$ at the class of $Q_n$ is the localization of the termwise exchange $b_n$ of Step 3 (the units $f_{*,n}\to Rf_{*,n}$, $h_{*,n}\to Rh_{*,n}$ are invertible by exactness). Its equation $T_{L_n}\nu_s^*(e_{L_n})=e^p_{\nu_X^*L_n}S_{L_n}$ then identifies $b_n$ with the canonical etale exchange, through the specified counit-normalized comparison. The etale exchange is invertible by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange]. This theorem for abelian sheaves also gives the module assertion: the restriction maps are $A_n$-linear, and an inverse to a bijective $A_n$-linear map is $A_n$-linear. All comparisons are natural, so transporting along $\alpha_n$ proves that $b_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism of pro-etale complexes.

For $h$ and $v^*L_n$, [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] supplies the canonical direct-image comparison and the inverse-image comparisons. The counit identity of [lem-pe-direct-image-mate-compatibility], applied to $h$, says exactly that its pro-etale counit, after this comparison and pullback, is $\nu_S^*$ of the etale counit. By [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived], applied to $h^*\dashv h_*$ on both sites with $h_*$ exact (Step 2), the derived counits are the localized termwise counits on every complex model; so the termwise counit used in Step 3 for $r_n$ is this derived pro-etale counit at the class of $v_n^*Q_n$, and the etale one is computed degreewise. Apply $i_x^*$ to this equality. The identity and composition equations of [lem-pe-inverse-image-comparison-coherence] identify the resulting sources by $hi_x=\mathrm{id}_s$ and the targets by $vi_x=x$. Thus the $x$-component of $r_n$ is the comparison image of the etale counit restriction at $i_x$. This identifies the actual component maps, rather than choosing an unrelated isomorphism of their endpoints. The statements apply to the bounded-below object $v_e^*L_n$, since inverse image is exact, and to $h$, which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The underived helper comparisonCounit is proved directly from mateEquiv_counit_symm and iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm, followed by cancellation of the inverse-image comparison isomorphism; no derived result is needed for this helper.

proof.text: For any etale module sheaf $F$ on $S$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction] to $h$ at $\mathrm{id}_s$. It gives the finite product of actual germs $(h_*F)_{\mathrm{id}_s}\simeq\prod_{x\in P_y}F_{i_x}$. The pointed identity neighbourhood $(s,\mathrm{id}_s)$ is initial in the category of pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\mathrm{id}_s$: its unique map to a pointed neighbourhood is the specified lift of that point. The opposite indexing category therefore has a terminal object. The categorical colimit lemma isIso_ι_of_isTerminal shows that the actual sections-to-stalk germ at the identity neighbourhood is invertible; this is the Lean helper etGerm_isIso and holds directly for module-valued sheaves. Thus the etale sheaf map with components $i_x^*\varepsilon_h$ is an isomorphism, and is identified on sections with the product-of-germs map just cited. The product is the direct sum since $P_y$ is finite. Apply this degreewise to a representative of $v_e^*L_n$, using exactness from Step 2 and, as in Step 7, [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived] to read the derived etale counit degreewise; then Step 7 transports this isomorphism to $r_n$. Thus $r_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism as a sheaf-complex map. If $P_y$ is empty, the same stalk formula has zero product in abelian groups, so the map to the zero complex is still a quasi-isomorphism.

The formulas in Steps 3-4 commute with every map of representatives: for a sheaf map $u$, $u(m|_\phi)=u(m)|_\phi$, and this equality holds in every degree. For a quasi-isomorphism $u:Q\to Q'$ between flat-term K-flat representatives, [lem-pur-change-of-rings-kflat-quasi-iso] makes each $u\otimes(A_n)_X$ a quasi-isomorphism. Step 2 and exact scalar restriction [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact] therefore make all three induced tower maps levelwise quasi-isomorphisms. The same constructions preserve chain homotopies, since they are additive termwise functors. To justify passage from representatives to all derived morphisms, [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] gives replacements, and [lem-pur-kflat-map-factorization] factors a map from a K-flat complex through a K-flat resolution of its target up to chain homotopy, retaining flat terms. Hence roofs may be computed with flat-term K-flat vertices, and two choices are compared after such refinements. Applying the strict naturality identities to the roofs and inverting their quasi-isomorphisms gives the same maps for every choice. Equivalently use the natural-transformation part of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. This proves naturality and representative independence in the derived categories of coefficient systems.

proof.text: In the abelian category of inverse systems of $R_s$-module sheaves, kernels, images and cokernels are computed levelwise: the transition on each kernel is the restriction of the given transition, and the transition on a cokernel is induced by its quotient universal property. Thus the cohomology of a complex of systems is also computed levelwise. Steps 6 and 8 say that both strict tower maps induce isomorphisms on this cohomology at every level; exact restriction of scalars preserves those assertions. By the definition of the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], they become isomorphisms in the derived category of systems. Applying exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] also shows that every evaluated $b_n$ and $r_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism, with precisely the etale section and point-restriction interpretations established in Steps 6-8.

source.place: Definition 05RU (definition-derived-category); levelwise kernels and cokernels in the category of systems; proetale.tex Tags 0982/098H for exact point sections

proof.text: Finally use the strict Roos model $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact, lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], the termwise products represent the derived products and their cohomology is the product of the cohomologies. Therefore the product of either family of levelwise quasi-isomorphisms is a quasi-isomorphism. The strict commuting squares of Step 4 give a square with the two $1-s$ maps, hence an actual map of their cone complexes. In the associated cone triangles the maps on the two product terms are isomorphisms in the derived category, so the cone map is an isomorphism as well (or apply the cohomology long exact sequences and the five lemma). Thus both total derived inverse-limit maps are isomorphisms. This argument uses the chosen strict systems; it requires no choice of a cone map from a bare morphism of towers in a triangulated category.

No new statements or holes are introduced; the remaining seven theorem proofs retain their plan.
